correctness.rationale: For all real angle perturbations and every radius 0<r<1, the boundary speed equals the Poisson sum, whose absolutely convergent Fourier series gives exact variance. The complete second-order expansion has two transverse DFT sectors; evaluating residue-class k² geometric series yields both rational coefficients, checked by independent exact-fraction identities. They are positive, and the reciprocal crossing polynomial maps to a cubic with exactly one root beyond four. Endpoint constants and analytic O_r(||h||³) follow from absolute summability of third derivatives. A standard-library script independently tests finite cases but is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Degree four is the first regular polygon with a two-dimensional first-Fourier perturbation type and a distinct alternating type. Knowing which displacements barely change the boundary speed is a natural quantitative robustness question for finite Blaschke circle coverings. The unique radius where these modes become isotropic and its exact algebraic threshold are not immediate from global extrema or uniform spacing, and give a complete local angular-stiffness classification at fixed radius, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
